items.title: ETH Zurich scientists turn WUJI robotic hand into self-propelled mobile manipulator
items.summary: ETH Zurich scientists demonstrated how a WUJI robotic hand can achieve self-propelled locomotion and manipulation without a separate mobility system. The research trained the hand to use its fingers for crawling, recovering from falls, and moving around its environment. This "compact mobile manipulator" was capable of performing self-supported tasks like pressing keyboard keys and pushing objects. Reinforcement learning was used to develop the locomotion, taking into account the unique characteristics of each finger. This work illustrates an unconventional approach by integrating locomotion and physical interaction capabilities into a single robotic hand.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, ETH Zurich scientists turn WUJI robotic hand into self-propelled mobile manipulator. This report details the demonstration of a WUJI robotic hand achieving self-propelled locomotion and manipulation without a separate mobility system. The research involved training the hand to utilize its fingers for crawling, recovering from falls, and navigating its surroundings. Reinforcement learning was employed to develop the locomotion by accounting for the unique characteristics of each finger, enabling the compact mobile manipulator to perform self-supported tasks such as pressing keyboard keys and pushing objects. This work integrates locomotion and physical interaction capabilities into a single robotic hand structure. This research suggests a novel pathway for developing highly mobile and interactive robotic systems in the future.

items.title: Tesla patent reveals touch-sensitive skin for robot hands
items.summary: Tesla filed a US patent for a touch-sensitive "skin" designed to mold around robot fingers and palms for detecting contact, force, and pressure. The patent describes a manufacturing process where tactile sensors are printed onto flexible materials and then heat-formed into three-dimensional shapes. The proposed sensor utilizes overlapping conductive regions on flexible substrate layers to register pressure changes through capacitive and piezoresistive methods. The technology emphasizes manufacturability using established techniques like screen printing and thermoforming for scalable production. This innovation aims to advance humanoid robots beyond basic grasping by enabling them to feel how firmly they are manipulating objects.

items.title: Skild AI trains robots to learn physical skills through self-play
items.summary: Skild AI developed a self-play training method using its S1 model to teach robots physical soccer skills through simulated competition. The robots learned complex behaviors like dribbling and tackling by playing against increasingly capable versions of themselves, rather than receiving explicit behavioral instructions. This method allowed the robots to develop skills from a single objective, leading to capabilities that emerged from the competitive process. After 140 years of simulation, the learned policy was successfully transferred to a physical humanoid robot. This approach aims to reduce the reliance on human demonstrations for teaching robots complex physical skills.

After 140 years of simulation, the resulting learned policy was successfully transferred to a physical humanoid robot, demonstrating a method to reduce reliance on human demonstrations for teaching robots complex physical abilities. This development signals a shift toward autonomous skill acquisition in robotics research.

items.title: The Sequence Robotics - Issue #952: One Brain, Many Bodies: Inside Skild AI's Robotics Bet
items.summary: Skild AI bets that robotic intelligence should be transferable across different hardware rather than being rebuilt for every machine. Their research focuses on connecting motor adaptation, video-prompted task learning, and self-play to achieve this goal. The core idea is to separate intelligence from the physical machine so that understanding a body is learned by the model. The company aims for the model to learn body understanding rather than requiring engineers to specify every detail perfectly beforehand. The ultimate test is whether these capabilities can survive the real-world requirements of speed, reliability, and safety in deployment.

The research involved connecting motor adaptation, video-prompted task learning, and self-play to achieve this goal. The methodology focuses on separating intelligence from the physical machine so that the model learns a generalized understanding of a body rather than requiring explicit prior engineering of every detail. The team aims for the model to acquire body understanding through experience. The ultimate assessment involves testing these capabilities against real-world demands for speed, reliability, and safety in deployment. This work suggests a pathway toward more adaptable and universally applicable artificial intelligence systems in robotics.

items.title: Pudu expands beyond service robots into semi-humanoids and quadrupeds
items.summary: Pudu Robotics is expanding its focus beyond service robots into developing semi-humanoid and quadruped robots. At IFA 2026, the company showcased these advancements, including the D7 semi-humanoid and the D5-W quadruped robot. The D7 focuses manipulation in its arms, waist, and head, capable of lifting up to 20 kg. The D5-W robot combines wheels and legs for varied terrain navigation and can autonomously recover from falls. This diversification extends Pudu's offerings and positions the company in competitive areas of industrial robotics.

items.title: Closing the Loop: How Automated Plants Turn Wastewater into Process Water
items.summary: Industrial water reuse involves treating effluent to be returned as process water, which can reduce fresh water consumption and discharge volume. Successful reuse requires a four-step process: diagnose water, engineer treatment, pilot the system, and deploy the full-scale system. Automation systems instrument the water loop using probes for conductivity, pH, and ORP, with a PLC controlling chemical dosing and water diversion. Recovered water is used for various applications like cooling tower makeup, washdown, or process feed, each with specific quality requirements. Implementing this system rewards the same control discipline used in production lines by measuring real input and proving performance before scaling.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, "Closing the Loop: How Automated Plants Turn Wastewater into Process Water". This story details the four-step process utilized by automated plants to treat industrial effluent into reusable process water, resulting in reduced freshwater consumption and discharge volume. The successful reuse process involves diagnosing the water, engineering the appropriate treatment, piloting the system, and finally deploying the full-scale system. Automation systems instrument the water loop using probes to measure conductivity, pH, and ORP, with a programmable logic controller managing chemical dosing and water diversion. Recovered water is subsequently applied to applications such as cooling tower makeup, washdown, or process feed, each requiring specific quality standards. Implementing these systems applies the control discipline from production lines by measuring actual input and verifying performance prior to scaling up operations. This advancement demonstrates the applicability of industrial control methodologies to complex environmental reclamation challenges.

items.title: Faraday Future launches $2,490 FF Nova humanoid for schools
items.summary: Faraday Future and FFR have launched the $2,490 FF Nova humanoid for schools, initially releasing only 100 invitation-only units. The Nova is a research and teaching platform measuring 49.7 cm and capable of walking, turning, and recovering from being knocked over. It features various sensors and supports ROS 2, with an additional software package available. A smaller, $299 Nova Mini is available for children, supporting visual block programming. The launch is part of a broader restructuring of the robotics business involving an acquisition.

items.title: An intelligent new shopping cart
items.summary: Google's Universal Cart is now available in the U.S. across Search and the Gemini app to simplify holiday shopping. It allows users to save products from multiple retailers into a single place, eliminating the need for multiple browser tabs. The cart actively tracks price drops, identifies relevant promo codes, and suggests payment methods. Users can complete purchases securely using Google Pay or transfer items directly to the merchant's site. This tool aims to give shoppers confidence and control over their online shopping experience.

This system allows users to consolidate products from various retailers into a single location, thereby eliminating the need for multiple browser tabs. The Universal Cart is integrated across Search and the Gemini application in the United States. It functions by actively tracking price fluctuations, identifying applicable promotional codes, and suggesting viable payment methods for the shopper. Purchases can be finalized securely through Google Pay or by directly transferring items to the merchant's website. This mechanism is intended to enhance shopper confidence and control during the online shopping process. The introduction of such integrated AI shopping assistance signals a trend toward more seamless and controlled digital commerce experiences.

items.title: PNDbotics Adam humanoid climbs 1 meter box, post claims
items.summary: PNDbotics' full-size Adam humanoid can climb onto a one-meter high box. This capability was detailed in a LinkedIn post by Space and Technology. The process involves the robot analyzing the obstacle, planning movements, and placing one foot on the box before shifting its weight. The climb requires the robot to support and raise its body while maintaining balance. The movement involves coordinated action across the entire body, with weight transfer being central to the ascent.

This ascent necessitated the robot supporting and raising its body while maintaining equilibrium, a process centered on the transfer of weight across the entire body structure. items.title: Hello Toronto! Waymo is En Route
items.summary: Waymo is launching its fully autonomous ride-hailing service in Toronto, aiming for first riders in 2028 through a phased, safety-first approach. The rollout will involve mapping local street networks and testing with autonomous specialists to ensure adaptation to Toronto's driving conditions. The expansion involves a partnership with Element Fleet Management to create jobs in fleet management, validation driving, and customer service. The Waymo Driver has been associated with significantly fewer serious accidents compared to human drivers based on autonomous driving data. The service aims to complement Toronto's existing transportation ecosystem while prioritizing safety and accessibility.

items.title: Causal Analysis of Robot Foundation Models Enables Efficiency Gains
items.summary: Causal analysis of vision-language-action (VLA) models investigates how perceptual and semantic representations are transformed into actions. The study found that causally relevant information influences the action expert through a specific "action-conditioning interface" in mid-to-late cross-attention layers. Restricting the action expert conditioning in one model reduced inference FLOPs by up to $33\%$ while maintaining task success. This principle was also demonstrated for real-robot deployment of other models. The research suggests that causal understanding can be directly used to improve the efficiency of robot foundation models.

items.title: Multi-Dimensional Featurizers Yield Fine-Grained Steering and Data Shaping in Robot Foundation Models
items.summary: Multi-dimensional featurizers, known as block-sparse featurizers (BSFs), are investigated to recover interpretable structure in robot foundation model features. These featurizers successfully capture task-relevant features such as perception, language, and proprioceptive state underlying the model's computation. Fine-grained steering experiments demonstrate that manipulating these features causally affects downstream action predictions. Furthermore, feature-based data attribution allows for isolating the specific training tokens responsible for observed behaviors like failure recovery. Overall, matching featurizers to representation geometry provides a more effective method for understanding and controlling robot behavior.

items.title: Feasibility Ceilings Before Learning: Sizing and Timing Bounds for Drone-Mesh Interception
items.summary: The paper establishes feasibility ceilings for drone-mesh interception before any learning policy is chosen. It provides closed-form bounds for performance based on the spread and timing of agents covering a predicted arrival point. Analysis shows that naive area ratios miss coverage ceilings, indicating constraints from separation, not the problem itself. Optimal packing is achieved by hexagonal arrangement, and other configurations yield less coverage. Analytic placement achieves 85% of the configuration's potential, while learned policies achieve significantly less, suggesting these bounds should guide learning experiments.

items.title: Persistent Profile-Guided Reset-Free Recovery Improves Final Gait Selection after Irreversible Leg Damage
items.summary: Persistent profile-guided reset-free recovery (PGRR) is introduced to improve final gait selection after irreversible leg damage. This method predicts multiple outcomes over repeated gait execution and uses uncertainty-aware estimates to guide short online probes without resetting the robot. Across 108 matched tasks involving leg amputation, fracture, and joint lock, PGRR improved final quality by 0.106 and slot-averaged recovery quality by 0.044 compared to a baseline. Furthermore, it reduced low-quality failures by 27.8 percentage points in all damage classes. Conservative uncertainty handling was identified as the clearest contributor to these performance gains.

items.title: Clarity-Driven Adaptive Mission Planning for a Solar-Powered Autonomous Surface Vessel
items.summary: A methodology is presented for adaptive mission planning for solar-powered autonomous surface vessels. This strategy maximizes the information-driven quantity of clarity, which is mathematically linked to differential entropy. The approach uses a clarity-driven ergodic search to adapt a target clarity map based on in-situ measurements. An ergodic path planner continually re-plans considering the target clarity map and mobility restrictions from the solar power source. Simulations at Jordan Lake demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach for such ASVs.

items.title: Race to Recovery: Designing Advanced Safety Systems for Autonomous Driving via Learning Autonomous Racing
items.summary: Existing safety systems fail when autonomous vehicles lose control due to events like icing or hydroplaning, as they focus on preventing instability rather than recovery. The research trains a racing policy using reinforcement learning to learn drifting as a time-optimal maneuver, then adapts it for recovery with a minimum-time reward. The method defines recovery based on a stable equilibrium and uses Gym-Khana for controller training and evaluation. This transferred policy significantly improves recovery over baseline methods and outperforms other controllers. The policy, when deployed on a physical vehicle, demonstrated the ability to recover from states the baseline could never handle.

items.title: Optimally Trading Energy for Information through Speed Trajectory Optimization of Sustainably Powered Mobile Robots
items.summary: Sustainably powered mobile robots can maximize information quality by optimizing their speed trajectories while managing energy. This involves solving a persistent, infinite-horizon speed trajectory optimization problem posed as a periodic optimal control problem. The study uses information-theoretic clarity as a metric to derive necessary conditions for optimal control, leading to follow-on properties characterizing the optimal speed choices. The research also establishes a high-speed information limit as energy reserves approach infinity. Simulation results, based on salinity characterization in the Chesapeake Bay, demonstrate the practical relevance of these optimized trajectories.

items.title: BubbleCBF: Constructive Safety for Second-Order Systems and Application to Autonomous Robot Navigation in Unknown Environments
items.summary: The research introduces BubbleCBF, a constructive method for designing feasible safety constraints for second-order control-affine systems. This involves constructing collision-free spheres, or "bubbles," from a signed distance function to define a velocity-dependent safety constraint. A quadratic-program safety filter is used to enforce the resulting safe set, which is represented by the overlap of these bubbles. The method proves the resulting controller is well-defined, continuous, and forward invariant under mild assumptions. The approach is demonstrated to achieve safe autonomous navigation for a differential-drive robot in unknown environments.
